title: Underactuated Thrust Decomposition & Horizontal Acceleration (欠驱动推力分解)
statement: A quadrotor (四旋翼 `sì xuán yì`) with mass $m = 1.5\text{ kg}$ maintains constant altitude while pitching forward by $\theta = 25^\circ$ ($g = 9.81\text{ m/s}^2$). (1) Why must an underactuated (欠驱动 `qiàn qū dòng`) quadrotor tilt to accelerate horizontally? (2) Compute the required total thrust $T$ (in $\text{N}$) and horizontal acceleration $a_h$ (in $\text{m/s}^2$), and compare $g\tan\theta$ against the small-angle approximation $g\theta$.
hints: Count the independent rotor thrust inputs vs. the 6 rigid-body degrees of freedom.
Because all 4 propellers point along body +z, vertical equilibrium requires T * cos(theta) = m * g while horizontal push is T * sin(theta).
Divide horizontal force by vertical force to obtain a_h = g * tan(25 deg), and convert 25 deg = 0.4363 rad for the small-angle comparison.
solution: (1) A quadrotor has 4 control inputs but 6 degrees of freedom (欠驱动 `qiàn qū dòng`), with all rotor thrust aligned with the body $z$-axis; thus it must tilt its body $z$-axis to project a horizontal force component $T\sin\theta$. (2) Holding altitude gives $T\cos 25^\circ = mg = 1.5 \times 9.81 = 14.715\text{ N} \Rightarrow T = 16.24\text{ N}$. Horizontal acceleration is $a_h = g\tan 25^\circ = 9.81 \times 0.4663 = 4.57\text{ m/s}^2$ (whereas small-angle $g\theta = 9.81 \times 0.4363 = 4.28\text{ m/s}^2$, a $6.3\%$ underestimate).

title: Unknown Payload Altitude Sag & Integral Action (未知载荷稳态下沉与积分作用)
statement: A $2.0\text{ kg}$ quadrotor picks up an unmodeled $\Delta m = 0.5\text{ kg}$ payload while hovering under a P-only vertical position/velocity controller with effective vertical stiffness $K_p = 6.0\text{ N/m}$ ($g = 9.81\text{ m/s}^2$). (1) Compute the extra weight force $\Delta F$ and the resulting steady-state altitude sag $e_{\text{ss}}$ (with units). (2) Why does doubling $K_p$ never reduce $e_{\text{ss}}$ to zero, and which PID term (积分项 `jī fēn xiàng`) eliminates the sag completely?
hints: Compute the extra downward gravity force dF = dm * g in Newtons first.
At steady hover under a P-only loop, the controller only produces extra thrust K_p * e_ss when a nonzero altitude error e_ss exists.
Check the units: N divided by (N/m) yields meters. Then consider what happens to an accumulated integral sum when error reaches zero.
solution: (1) Extra weight: $\Delta F = \Delta m \cdot g = 0.5\text{ kg} \times 9.81\text{ m/s}^2 = 4.905\text{ N}$. Steady-state balance requires $K_p e_{\text{ss}} = \Delta F \Rightarrow e_{\text{ss}} = 4.905\text{ N} / (6.0\text{ N/m}) = 0.8175\text{ m} \approx 0.82\text{ m}$. (2) A P-only term outputs $u_P = K_p e$, which vanishes if $e = 0$; doubling $K_p$ halves the sag to $0.41\text{ m}$ but cannot hold $4.905\text{ N}$ at $e = 0$. Adding integral action $K_i \int e\,dt$ (积分项 `jī fēn xiàng`) stores the accumulated error history so it continues outputting $+4.905\text{ N}$ after $e \to 0\text{ m}$.

title: Cascaded PID Loop Hierarchy & Tuning Order (串级PID内外环关系与整定顺序)
statement: In the quadrotor cascaded flight controller (`StabilizerTask.c`), four nested loops run from outer to inner: position (位置环 `wèi zhì huán`), velocity (速度环 `sù dù huán`), attitude (姿态环 `zī tài huán`), and angular rate (角速度环 `jiǎo sù dù huán`). (1) Write the exact Chinese hierarchy sentences connecting rate, attitude, and velocity loops using the `A是B的C` pattern. (2) If the inner attitude loop has a $0.27\text{ s}$ phase lag while the outer velocity loop aggressively commands tilt on a figure-8 path, what flight signature appears and which loop must be tuned first?
hints: In Chinese `A是B的内环` means A is the inner loop of B (do not reverse into 内环的B).
Rate (角速度环) sits inside attitude (姿态环), which sits inside velocity (速度环).
When the inner loop lags the outer command by 0.27 s near the figure-8 lobe frequency, the delay erodes phase margin and amplifies the trajectory (overshoot).
solution: (1) Chinese hierarchy: **角速度环是姿态环的内环，姿态环是速度环的内环。先调内环，后调外环。** (2) Because the outer velocity loop relies on the inner attitude/rate loops to realize commanded tilt angles almost instantaneously ($\tau_{\text{inner}} \ll \tau_{\text{outer}}$), a $0.27\text{ s}$ inner attitude lag causes late push and phase-lag amplification (flying the figure-8 lobes $17\text{–}28\%$ too wide with overshoot). You must always tune from the innermost loop outward (先调角速度环，再调姿态环，最后调速度环和位置环).

title: 2-DOF Feed-Forward vs. MRAC Reference Model Bandwidth (前馈控制与模型参考自适应带宽)
statement: A quadrotor tracks a figure-8 trajectory where $x(t)$ oscillates at $2\omega$ and $y(t)$ at $\omega$. (1) Why does scaling a velocity feed-forward (前馈 `qián kuì`) gain by $1.2\times$ worsen RMS tracking error when the real issue is inner-loop phase lag, and what does a model-inverse feed-forward $u_{\text{ff}} = r + (2\zeta/\omega_n)\dot{r} + \ddot{r}/\omega_n^2$ do instead? (2) In `lqr-track`, if the baseline LQR closes the loop at $\omega_{\text{LQR}} \approx 4.8\text{ rad/s}$ but the MRAC reference model is left at $\omega_m = 2.0\text{ rad/s}$, how does MRAC react and what distinguishes $\omega_m$ from the adaptation rate $\Gamma$?
hints: Separate amplitude scaling from timing/phase lead: multiplying velocity FF by 1.2 changes size, not the phase delay.
Model-inverse FF supplies the derivatives (velocity + acceleration) needed to cancel the nominal plant's phase lag at every instant.
In MRAC, the tracking error is e = x - x_ref. If the baseline LQR (4.8 rad/s) responds faster than x_ref (2.0 rad/s), what sign does e have, and what does MRAC adapt toward?
solution: (1) Scaling velocity FF gain by $1.2\times$ inflates command amplitude without fixing timing lag, increasing figure-8 RMS error. Model-inverse 2-DOF feed-forward ($r + (2\zeta/\omega_n)\dot{r} + \ddot{r}/\omega_n^2$, i.e., position + velocity + acceleration FF) provides the phase lead required by the nominal plant dynamics so feedback only handles disturbances and model mismatch. (2) In MRAC, $\omega_m$ defines the **target reference trajectory** $x_{\text{ref}}(t)$, whereas $\Gamma$ sets the **adaptation speed** (learning rate). When $\omega_m = 2.0\text{ rad/s} < \omega_{\text{LQR}} \approx 4.8\text{ rad/s}$, the plant responds faster than $x_{\text{ref}}$, creating a nonzero error $e = x - x_{\text{ref}}$ that causes MRAC to actively fight LQR and slow the closed-loop response down toward $2.0\text{ rad/s}$ (fixed in `lqr-plus-mrac` by matching $\omega_m = 4.8\text{ rad/s}$).
